audit.title: Audit trail
personal-data.title: Personal data access
personal-data.recorded.text:
Values are shown masked first; a person who may see them whole reveals them with a reason. Every reveal is audited as `records_viewed` with:

- its **purpose**, from a fixed list, and its **reference** (a ticket or case number) when one was given;
- its **job**, how many **rows** it showed and the **names of the fields** it showed: never a value.

Views audited before reveals asked for a reason have none of these and read as *not recorded*. A masked read is not a view and is not listed. There is no way to export personal data. A view is known by its resource and its shape, **not by which clients** it showed.

runs.stages: Time per stage of the evaluation
runs.not_yet.text: The time per stage is all the workers report today: **bytes read and spilled per stage** are still to come (`0020_job_stats.sql`). A finished job keeps no worker: the queue clears it, so _Worker slot_ is filled only while a job runs. Open a run's **cut** to see its logs.
run-logs.title: Logs by run
run-logs.matching.text: Lines are matched by the **run's id** (`run_id`, its cut's id) or **one of its jobs' ids** (its extraction and its evaluation, `job_id`), as text, in any service of the platform over the time range shown. The API and the worker log these ids as fields; matching their text also finds older lines and other services' lines that name them (such as Traefik's access log of the worker's calls), and shows a line that names one for another reason. The run's id is shared by the cut's replacement runs, so their lines are shown too; only the latest run's jobs are listed. The observability stack's own lines (Grafana, Loki, Alloy) are left out: they log the search itself.
